scope: Native base-10 Sint_to_buf, write_big_simple/D_div and integer_to_binary/1. Explicit selection of the schoolbook algorithm, not partial admission of write_big's D&C dispatch.
adaptations: Base-10 native flat-64 lookup entries are 17 digits and divisor 10^17. D_div's original quotient/remainder loop uses bounded indices instead of forming pre-allocation pointers.
One fallible domain allocation owns the continuation, copied limbs and output bytes. A checked 20 bytes per 64-bit limb plus sign replaces floating-point size estimation.

The sole formatting algorithm is native schoolbook division with resumable state between complete division passes. D&C, Barrett, Karatsuba and dirty-scheduler infrastructure are not linked or claimed; full canonical native integer values are formatted without truncation.
A worker call processes 4096 limb-work units, overrunning by at most one native limb vector. Actual work charges reductions. This is not a hard timing or throughput guarantee.

Only integer_to_binary/1 can retain the typed process-owned decimal continuation. The existing native trampoline resumes it; no synthetic bytecode, host-side guest execution, dirty pool or generic trapping-BIF capability is introduced.
Completion builds the existing owned heap/offheap binary after fallible collection. Scratch is released on completion, OOM and physical process destruction, including cancellation and world stop.
Small signed formatting uses unsigned magnitude to avoid signed-negation overflow at INT64_MIN. No other base, integer parser or integer_to_binary/2 admission follows.
